title: latent-reserve-cushion-autoscale-prd-draft
body:
Purpose
---
This is an early PRD describing a complementary autoscaling primitive for Dedicated capacity: the "latent reserve cushion" (LRC). The LRC is a small, continuously provisioned pool of dormant (low-power/idle) instances that can be rapidly activated to absorb short, high-priority surges while preserving tenant isolation and predictable unit economics.

Problem statement
---
- Dedicated customers want predictable baseline capacity but need safe, fast burst options for spikes (marketing campaigns, traffic surges, scheduled batch workloads).
- Existing burst mechanisms either: 1) overcommit and risk noisy neighbors, or 2) require long warmup (coldstart) which violates latency SLOs.
- We need an autoscale design that provides quick capacity with explicit isolation controls and clear cost allocation back to tenants.

Goals
---
- Provide <30s activation for small bursts (up to X GPU-equivalents per tenant) without degrading baseline tenant SLOs.
- Minimize steady-state cost for customers and Redwood by keeping LRC size small and adaptive.
- Offer explicit tenant guardrails: soft-fence, chargeback ledger, and graceful demotion path.
- Integrate with existing Dedicated reservation model and billing.

Non-goals
---
- This PRD does not replace large-scale autoscaling (minutes-scale pool growth) for sustained demand.
- Not proposing a full spot-market for Dedicated (that is separate).

Concept overview
---
Core idea: keep a geographically/zone-balanced collection of warm-but-dormant GPU nodes (LRC nodes). Each node has a low-power idle state (minimal memory residency, quick kernel priming maintained). A tenant request for burst first consults policy: if eligible, we allocate capacity from the tenant's "cushion credit" and instantiate request routing to an LRC-backed runtime.

Key primitives
- Cushion pool: global set of N LRC nodes per region (configurable per account size).
- Cushion credits: per-tenant accounting tokens that determine how much of the cushion a tenant may consume without approval. Credits replenish over time or via pre-purchase.
- Soft-fence: tenant-level cap and CPU/GPU QoS cgroups applied to LRC-allocated workloads to prevent cross-tenant interference.
- Eviction parity: clear metrics and compensation policy (credits returned / partial refunds) if tenant burst causes evictions or degrades baseline SLOs.
- Fast-priming path: maintain minimal model shard residency and precompiled kernels for common models to reduce activation time.

Autoscale behavior
---
1) Normal: Dedicated pool serves baseline traffic. LRC nodes remain idle but primed.
2) Surge: Tenant traffic spikes. Router checks cushion credits and activation policy. If within policy, route to LRC node.
3) Activation: switch completes in target <= 30s, with KV cache warmed opportunistically from snapshot store.
4) Decay: after surge, workloads are gently migrated back to baseline or kept on LRC for a configurable grace window. Credits are debited.

Policy examples (draft)
---
- Small tenant: cushion_credit = 2 GPU-minutes/sec replenishes 5% per hour. Burst cap = 1 GPU for up to 10 minutes per day.
- Mid tenant: cushion_credit = 10 GPU-minutes, replenishes 20% per hour, burst cap = 4 GPUs up to 30 minutes.
- Enterprise: large credits with approval, multi-GPU bursts, can reserve extra LRC slices for a fee.

Isolation controls
---
- Soft-Fence QoS: enforce per-tenant token bucket on GPU cycles + memory bandwidth throttles where supported.
- Affinity tagging: ensure LRC-backed workloads are scheduled on nodes with strict hypervisor limits to contain noisy neighbor effects.
- Preflight validation: a lightweight perf-sim that rejects allocations likely to exceed allowed tail-latency impact (runs within <500ms).

Cost & chargeback model (rough math)
---
- Baseline LRC cost: assume 10 LRC nodes regionally, 24/7 idle cost = 10 * $X/day. Spread across customers as a subscription fee + usage debits.
- Example: if one LRC node idle = $20/day, 10 nodes = $200/day; amortize across 50 customers = $4/customer/day baseline. Burst usage billed per-GPU-minute at 1.5x hosted rate (covers readiness premium).
- Need FP review with finance for tax/invoicing implications.

Observability & SLOs
---
- New metrics: cushion_activation_time_p50/p95, cushion_utilization_by_tenant, cushion_credit_balance, cushion_eviction_events.
- Alerts: activation latency p95 > 45s, cushion_eviction_rate > 0.5% per hour.
- Add to Console: per-route cushion usage, chargeback preview, burst heatmap.

Operational runbook (high level)
---
- Day-2 ops: monitor cushion_utilization and historical peak correlation; when utilization > 70% sustained, schedule LRC scale-out (operator or autoscale rule).
- Incident: if cushion activations cause baseline SLO violations, soft-stop new activations and throttle by percent; notify affected tenants with automated message + credit remediation.
- RCA: capture pre-activation traces and KV cache deltas.

Simulator & validation plan
---
- Build a stochastic simulator to model: tenant mix, burst arrival processes, cushion sizing, and credit decay. Use historical traffic from 3 pilot tenants.
- Key outputs: probability of contention leading to baseline SLO impact, cost per-tenant, optimal cushion sizing per region.

Rollout plan (phased)
---
1) Internal pilot: enable on internal+canary tenants, observe activation latencies and eviction signals (2–4 weeks).
2) Beta: offer to 5 willing customers with manual enablement and higher chargeback rates.
3) GA: automated billing integration, self-serve controls in Console, RBAC for enabling.

Open questions / risks
---
- How to implement low-power idle while preserving kernel/compilation priming? HW vendor constraints.
- Billing UX: pre-purchase credits vs pay-as-you-go — which reduces churn friction?
- Legal/regulatory: can we auto-charge cushion usage for regulated customers under existing contracts?
- Edge cases: long-lived bursts that push the cushion into sustained usage — fallback to normal autoscale or require reserve purchase?

Next steps / TODOs
---
- Engineering: prototype LRC node lifecycle (idle priming, activation API) — owner: eng-serving-runtime (Ethan).
- Product: draft pricing tiers and credit replenishment curves — owner: Maya.
- Research: run warmup experiments for top 10 customer models and publish priming cost matrix — owner: applied-ml (Priya).
- Finance/legal: validate billing language and contract impact — owner: finance-and-legal (Jon).
- Create simulator JIRA and link to this doc.

Notes to reviewers
---
- This is intentionally exploratory: many policy knobs proposed to understand tradeoffs. Looking for feedback on acceptable activation time targets, pricing roughs, and whether we should tie cushion credits to monthly committed spend.
- Slack thread with initial design discussion: #dedicated-lrc (see pinned messages).

References
---
- Related ideas: idle-pool-reclamation playbook, prewarm orchestrator notes (see linked artifacts).
- Perf experiments and kernel priming notes (applied-ml internal notebook).

Unresolved items for next sync
---
- Decide default cushion sizing heuristic for new customers.
- Finalize eviction compensation policy (refund vs credit vs SLA credit).
- Determine if LRC should be offered in Private deployments or limited to Redwood-managed Dedicated only.

-- End of draft --
